title: English Teaching Jobs in Vietnam: 7 Types Compared (2026)
description: Language centres, public schools via agencies, kindergartens, bilingual and international schools, universities, corporate: hours, pay and rules in HCMC.
h1: English teaching jobs in Vietnam: the seven kinds of employer, compared
intro: Private language centres are the most numerous employers of foreign English teachers in Vietnam and the usual first job: hourly pay, weekday-evening and weekend classes, mostly children and teens. The alternatives are agency-run public-school programmes (weekday daytime, September to May), kindergartens, bilingual and international schools (monthly salaries, stricter credentials), universities and corporate training. This guide compares all seven in Ho Chi Minh City as of October 2026.
keyPoints: **Language centres** are the usual first job: July–October 2026 ads offered {{vnd:390000-600000}} an hour, most new-teacher offers {{vnd:430000-560000}}, for 20–25 hours a week of mostly evening and weekend classes.
**Public-school agency work** is weekday daytime at {{vnd:430000-600000}} an hour in 2025–2026 ads, but it follows the school year, so hourly pay largely stops from June to August.
**Kindergartens** run in the morning and daytime; MOET's kindergarten programme asks native-speaker teachers for 120 hours of early-childhood training on top of a degree and a teaching certificate.
**Bilingual and international schools** pay monthly salaries and ask for more: international schools usually want a home-country teaching licence, which a TEFL does not replace.
**Universities and corporate English** are small markets: RMIT asks for CELTA plus 3 years' post-CELTA experience, and published corporate rates are scarce.

Whatever the employer, teachers are usually permitted as 'experts' (a bachelor's degree plus 2 years' relevant experience), and teaching before the permit is issued risks a {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} fine and deportation.

sections.title: The seven kinds of English teaching job, compared

blocks.text: Ho Chi Minh City is Vietnam's biggest market for foreign English teachers. In August 2025 it had [1,961 licensed foreign-language and IT centres](https://daibieunhandan.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-nang-cao-chat-luong-nhan-su-tai-cac-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tin-hoc-10388655.html), 158 of them foreign-invested, and 2,093 of its 5,593 kindergartens offered English familiarisation. Add public schools, bilingual and international schools, universities and companies, and the real choice is which kind of working week you want.

sections.title: Language centres, public schools and kindergartens: what the work is like

blocks.text: Language centres: the usual first job

Centres are by far the most numerous employers, and the big chains include VUS, ILA and Apollo English. [VUS describes the standard deal](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/?p=979): classes mostly for 6–16-year-olds on weekday evenings and all day at weekends, 20–25 hours a week full-time or 12–18 part-time, a first month of observed teaching at full hourly pay as probation, then a 12-month contract once probation is passed and the work permit is issued. That probation month is paid work too, so your permit must be issued before it starts.

A full-time centre load (about 78–95 contact hours a month in a 2024 Apollo listing) at {{vnd:450000-550000}} an hour works out at roughly {{vnd:35000000-52000000}} gross a month before tax and insurance. Figures such as [ILA's 'average income up to'](https://www.eslbase.com/job/hiring-esl-teachers-in-vietnam-over-70-centres-and-30-years-of-experience-8/) {{vnd:500000}} an hour for new teachers are ceilings, not starting rates. The British Council, at the top of the market, runs [six teaching centres in the city](https://britishcouncil.vn/en/english-courses/teaching-centre/tan-binh), mostly for learners aged 3–17, and has asked for CELTA, Trinity CertTESOL or equivalent; its teacher vacancies appear only irregularly.

The catch is churn. The city [dissolved or revoked 112 language and IT centres](https://vietnamnet.vn/en/ho-chi-minh-city-shuts-down-112-language-and-it-centers-2556885.html) in 2025–26, and the [Apax Leaders chain collapsed](https://vietnamfinance.vn/he-thong-te-liet-va-giai-the-apax-leaders-dang-no-ca-tram-ty-dong-d108066.html) owing teachers' wages. Ask current teachers whether pay has been on time before you sign. The centre week in detail is in [working at a language centre in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/language-centre-jobs-in-ho-chi-minh-city).
Public school programmes through agencies

Foreign teachers in public schools are usually placed by education companies, usually called agencies, rather than hired by the school. They teach fee-paying 'linked' English classes, which HCMC says must be [voluntary for families](https://giaoducthudo.giaoducthoidai.vn/chuong-trinh-lien-ket-o-tphcm-khong-phai-cu-duoc-phep-la-dua-vao-truong-223264.html), or programmes such as the city's integrated maths, science and English programme (Đề án 5695), which [reported over 40,000 students](https://www.sggp.org.vn/dua-tieng-anh-thanh-ngon-ngu-thu-hai-trong-truong-hoc-post764562.html) at the end of 2023–24 and relies on foreign teachers.

The week is weekday daytime and the year is the school year: HCMC students [report on 24 August](https://thanhnien.vn/tphcm-cong-bo-ngay-tuu-truong-khai-giang-nam-hoc-2026-2027-va-cac-nam-tiep-theo-185260812151153867.htm) (17 August for first and final grades) and the year ends before 31 May. [GEMS advertised](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/foreign-esl-teachers-for-public-schools-in-ho-chi-minh-city-2026-2027/) {{vnd:430000-480000}} an hour for Grades 1–5 and asked teachers to bring their own laptop. [DTP offered](https://teast.co/job/part-time-english-teacher-ho-chi-minh-city-vietnam-7Qmx5WWpL4QLXDXiQKO2) up to {{vnd:550000}} an hour for at least 3 weekdays, sponsored part of the work-permit cost and wanted proof you are already in Vietnam.

Expect big classes. The legal caps are [35 pupils in primary and 45 in secondary](https://luatvietnam.vn/linh-vuc-khac/si-so-lop-hoc-883-91779-article.html), HCMC primary classes [averaged 38 in 2022](https://vnexpress.net/truong-cong-qua-tai-4507502.html), and a Vietnamese co-teacher is usually in the room. Periods last 35 minutes at primary and 45 at secondary, so ask whether you are paid per 60-minute hour or per period.

HCMC has tightened the paperwork. A [January 2024 directive](https://voh.com.vn/giao-duc/trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tai-tphcm-khong-duoc-thu-hoc-phi-dai-han-510985.html) requires centres sending foreign teachers into schools to provide each teacher's work permit before the teacher starts, and since [January 2026](https://daibieunhandan.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-ra-soat-nang-luc-bang-cap-giao-vien-chuong-trinh-lien-ket-10402625.html) schools running linked programmes must hold a full file for every foreign teacher, including certified translations of degree and certificates and a work permit naming the English-teacher role and an HCMC workplace. Ask the agency who your legal employer and work-permit sponsor is. One agency contract reported in Hanoi [fined the school](https://giaoduc.net.vn/nhon-nhip-thi-truong-cho-thue-giao-vien-nuoc-ngoai-day-tieng-anh-lien-ket-o-truong-cong-post255408.gd) {{vnd:20000000}} for each teacher it hired directly.

A June 2026 HCMC pilot lets [246 public preschools and schools](https://giaoduc.net.vn/tphcm-246-truong-mam-non-pho-thong-duoc-tu-tuyen-giao-vien-hop-dong-voi-giao-vien-nuoc-ngoai-post260905.gd) sign contracts with foreign teachers directly from 2026 to 2030. No such direct-hire ads had appeared by October 2026, and the pilot sets no new qualification standards, so the usual permit rules still apply.
Kindergartens

Kindergarten English is short, frequent sessions. Under [Circular 50/2020](https://luatvietnam.vn/tin-van-ban-moi/to-chuc-cho-tre-mau-giao-lam-quen-voi-tieng-anh-35-tuan-nam-186-29560-article.html) it runs 35 weeks a year with at least two 25–35-minute activities a week. HCMC is also piloting [integrated English in public kindergartens](https://giaoducthoidai.vn/tphcm-trien-khai-tieng-anh-tich-hop-bac-mam-non-tren-nguyen-tac-tu-nguyen-post794467.html) for three years from 2026–27, with the provider supplying foreign teachers: 4 activities a week for ages 3–5 and 6 for ages 5–6.

Part-time slots are often a few short classes on a few mornings: [one Tan Binh kindergarten](https://teast.co/job/part-time-esl-teacher-for-kindergarten-dIUfG4eZOchx6u9HEJzC) offered {{vnd:420000-450000}} an hour for two 30-minute classes on three mornings a week. Full-time homeroom posts fill the school day: [an EIV homeroom role in Go Vap](https://teast.co/job/full-time-homeroom-kindergarten-teacher-go-vap-district-Ow6XNeTaalIIPg66rO3U) ran Monday to Friday 7:30–17:00 for up to {{vnd:48000000}} a month, with social and health insurance support and paid holidays.

For MOET's kindergarten programme, native-speaker teachers need a college degree or higher, a recognised English-teaching certificate and at least 120 hours of early-childhood training, including 45 practical hours at a preschool. Ads asking for 'native speakers aged 23–40' state an employer preference, not the law. Classroom technique for this age group is in [teaching young learners and kindergarten](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-young-learners-in-vietnam).

sections.title: Bilingual and international schools: salaried, stricter, hired earlier

blocks.text: Bilingual and private 'international programme' schools
These private schools hire foreign teachers on monthly salaries for homeroom or subject teaching. In September–October 2026 ads they offered US$1,700–3,000 a month.

[Pathway School in Thu Thiem](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/expat-primary-teacher-pathway-school-district-2-hcmc-full-time) offered US$1,900–2,350 a month gross with compulsory social and health insurance, for 30–34 periods of 35 minutes a week, Monday to Friday 7:00–17:00, plus 12 days' annual leave, a 6-day paid summer break and both Vietnamese and home-country holidays. Requirements vary widely: [SSG Education in Binh Thanh](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/primary-mathscience-and-ela-teachers-starting-august-2026) asked for a B.Ed, PGCE, QTS or US licence and 2 years' experience. Teaching maths or science in English brings its own legal requirements (see the table below).
International schools

Premium international schools pay licensed teachers about US$2,500–4,000+ a month, usually with housing support, annual flights and medical cover. [One recruiter's ad](https://teachanywhere.com/jobs/secondary-english-teacher-aug-2025-hcmc-vietnam_ho-chi-minh-city_44373153) for a British-curriculum school offered 2-year contracts. Housing support varies a lot from school to school, so compare whole packages.

They hire on credentials a TEFL cannot replace. [Saigon South International School](https://search.openapply.com/schools/saigon-south-international-school) normally wants a master's degree, 2 years' successful teaching and a home-country licence, and [ISHCMC](https://www.ishcmc.com/who-we-are/careers/) says all its teachers are certified for the IB programmes. The law sets a floor too: at foreign-invested general schools, teachers need at least a [university pedagogy degree or equivalent](https://vcci.com.vn/legal-document/nghi-dinh-862018nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-hop-tac-dau-tu-cua-nuoc-ngoai-trong-linh-vuc-giao-duc).

The big schools recruit through group portals (Cognita, Nord Anglia) and international boards such as Schrole, TES and Search Associates rather than local ads. Teachers commonly have their licence, references and recruiter profiles ready by September–October for the following August. Check a school's standing as well as its brochure: [American International School Vietnam](https://tuoitre.vn/nld/american-international-school-officially-dissolved-196260114102410854.htm) was dissolved in January 2026, and the city ordered it to settle staff salaries and overdue insurance. More in [international school jobs in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/international-school-jobs-in-vietnam).

sections.title: Universities and corporate English: adult learners, fewer jobs

blocks.text: Universities

University English jobs are few and the bar is high. [RMIT Vietnam's 2026 'Educator' role](https://www.rmit.edu.au/content/dam/rmit/au/en/careers/position-descriptions/vietnam/JD-Educator%20July%202026.pdf) in its School of English and University Pathways is paid by the hour and asks for a bachelor's degree, CELTA or equivalent and at least 3 years' verifiable post-CELTA experience, with a relevant master's desirable. Non-native speakers need IELTS Academic 8.0 with no band below 7.5.

RMIT's last published rate, in an ad that closed in December 2023, was [US$30.55 gross per teaching hour](https://vn.linkedin.com/jobs/view/english-language-educators-hourly-hcmc-hanoi-and-danang-at-rmit-university-3673867344), with no guaranteed hours: teaching depended on enrolments and there could be none in some periods. There are no verified current pay figures for public universities, so judge any offer on the written terms.

The legal floor is low: native-speaker lecturers teaching language skills at foreign-invested universities need a bachelor's degree or higher. Employers ask more: [TEFL Org](https://www.tefl.org/teach-english-abroad/teach-english-in-vietnam/) says universities generally want a master's or PhD, and the International University (VNU-HCM) asked for one for visiting English lecturers in 2024.
Corporate and business English

Corporate work means teaching staff at client companies, often arranged through training providers and teacher-supply companies. Published rates are scarce. [One HCMC teacher-supply company's 2026 price list](https://byan.com.vn/vn/bang-gia-cung-cap-giao-vien-nuoc-ngoai) charges clients {{vnd:800000-1000000}} an hour for corporate training, and the teacher receives less after the agency's margin. The only teacher-side figure found is older: a [Hanoi business-English provider](https://teast.co/job/business-english-and-soft-skills-trainer-RUBQp07uuQ8zqbkQdxZu) paid {{vnd:600000-700000}} an hour before tax around 2024, starting at 6.5 hours a month, with an allowance for off-site projects.

With hours that small, corporate classes work best as a top-up to a centre or school job. If a provider offers you corporate hours, ask who holds your work permit and whether the role and workplace on it cover teaching at client sites: work that does not match the permit costs the employer {{vnd:5000000-10000000}} per worker, doubled for a company, under [Decree 283/2026/ND-CP](https://www.vietnam-briefing.com/news/vietnam-foreign-worker-penalties-under-decree-283.html/).

sections.title: Where IELTS centres, private tutoring and online teaching fit

blocks.text: IELTS preparation is a specialism inside the centre market rather than a separate kind of employer, and much of its demand comes from students using IELTS for university admission. That demand is at risk: Vietnam had about 300,000 IELTS test sessions in 2025, but a [MOET draft published on 17 September 2026](https://tienphong.vn/bo-cong-diem-chung-chi-ielts-mieng-banh-nghin-ti-se-ra-sao-post1879043.tpo), still a draft in October 2026, would end bonus points for language certificates in university admissions from 2027. IDP's ACET academic English and IELTS centres [closed on 31 December 2024](https://www.idp.com/vietnam/blog/official-acet-announcement/?lang=en). Ask what share of your hours would be IELTS before building a career on it; see [teaching IELTS in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-ielts-in-vietnam).

Online platforms pay far less than classroom work: [Cambly pays tutors](https://support.cambly.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055993652-Prospective-Tutors-FAQs) US$10.20 an hour on its standard platform, with no guaranteed hours. Treat platforms abroad as a top-up at most: teaching online for a company abroad while living here is a legal grey area, and a Vietnam-based platform needs a work permit for you. Paid private students are not a lawful top-up. Your work permit covers only the employer and workplaces named on it, and there is no freelance-tutor route for a foreigner, so cash lessons risk a {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} fine and deportation (Decree 283/2026/ND-CP). Rates and rules are in [private tutoring and online teaching in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/private-tutoring-and-online-teaching-in-vietnam).

sections.title: What the law asks of each employer type

blocks.text: Employers usually ask for more than the law does, and the legal floor differs by setting. The work permit sits on top of all of them.

blocks.caption: Legal minimum for foreign English teachers by setting (Vietnamese regulations in force, October 2026)
rows: College degree or higher in any field plus a 'suitable' teaching certificate; no minimum course hours
As above plus Level 5 (about CEFR C1) proof, unless the degree is in English or in teaching it
Integrated programme (subjects such as maths and science in English)
University degree matching the subject, a pedagogy certificate or equivalent, and Level 5 English
At least a university pedagogy degree or equivalent
College degree or higher, recognised English-teaching certificate, 120 hours of early-childhood training (45 practical)

blocks.text: The work permit is the real gate. Teachers are usually filed as 'experts' under [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html), in force since 7 August 2025, which replaced Decrees 152/2020 and 70/2023. An expert needs a bachelor's degree or higher plus at least 2 years of relevant work experience, usually proved by a letter from a past employer abroad; experience in Vietnam counts only through earlier Vietnamese work permits. For experts in education, the decree also lists documents showing you meet the qualification standard set by education law as an alternative proof, but how Ho Chi Minh City applies that to a teacher with under 2 years' experience is not published.

If you have less than 2 years' experience, ask the employer which proof they will file for you and get the answer in writing before you travel. [A TEFL, TESOL or CELTA](/teach-in-vietnam/tefl-tesol-and-celta-for-vietnam) does not replace the degree, and on its own it does not replace the experience: it is the education-side requirement, MOET guidance accepts [internationally accredited certificates](https://luatvietnam.vn/linh-vuc-khac/trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-thue-giao-vien-nuoc-ngoai-can-dieu-kien-gi-883-100926-article.html), and '120 hours' is an employer convention. The full procedure is in the [work permit guide for English teachers](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers); your employer and the authority have the final word.

Do not start teaching before the permit is issued, whatever the employer says. Since 10 September 2026, [Decree 283/2026/ND-CP](https://news.tuoitre.vn/foreign-workers-in-vietnam-what-to-know-as-new-penalty-rules-take-effect-september-10-103260824152235374.htm) fines a foreigner working without one {{vnd:15000000-25000000}}, and the worker may be deported.

sections.title: How to choose, and when each type hires

blocks.text: Language centres hire all year, busiest June to August and slowest from mid-December to Tet; public-school agencies recruit in June to August for a September start; international schools recruit many months ahead of an August start. The full hiring calendar, and how long a search takes, is in [finding a teaching job in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/finding-a-teaching-job-in-vietnam#when-schools-hire).

items: **Daytime hours, evenings free:** public-school agency work, kindergartens or bilingual schools. Agency pay is hourly and follows the school year.
**Steadiest income:** a salaried school post. On a contract of 12 months or more, compulsory social insurance takes 9.5% of your salary, so compare offers net to net.
**New, with a degree and a TEFL:** a chain centre is the usual first job. The international-school route needs a teaching licence first.

**Non-native speaker:** at centres the law asks for Level 5 (C1) proof unless your degree is in English or English teaching. Some employers list 'native' English as a requirement; VUS considers non-native applicants who send an intro video.
**Adults rather than children:** evening adult and IELTS classes at centres, corporate hours as a top-up, or a university post once you have CELTA and several years' experience.

blocks.title: Hourly pay is only as good as the hours
blocks.text: The most common bad surprise is a good hourly rate with too few hours. Hourly arrangements often pay nothing for cancelled classes, Tet closures or the June–August public-school summer, and 'up to' rates are ceilings. Before you sign, get the guaranteed minimum hours or pay a month in writing, and ask whether the rate is gross or net and per 60-minute hour or per period. What else to check is in [English teaching contracts in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teaching-contracts-in-vietnam).

To see who is hiring now, [eno.vn's teaching jobs page](/jobs-vietnam-expats) gathers postings from job boards and schools' careers pages; a linked posting opens the original, where you apply, and eno.vn has not verified the employers behind them. The [Saigon school directory](/schools) lists Ho Chi Minh City employers by type (language centres, international and bilingual schools, teacher agencies and universities), where teachers who worked or interviewed there can leave reviews; most have few or none yet.

Never pay anyone to get a teaching job: [VUS warns](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/fake-job-warning) that any request for money or to download an app is a scam. And check where an 'HCMC' job really is. Since 1 July 2025 the city has included the former [Binh Duong and Ba Ria–Vung Tau provinces](https://en.vneconomy.vn/hcm-city-ready-for-operation-of-new-government-apparatus-from-july-1.htm), so a campus can be one to two hours from District 1. Ads still use the old district names, while official addresses now use new ward names.

faqs.q: Can I teach English in Vietnam without a degree?
faqs.a: Not on the usual legal route. Teachers are normally permitted as experts, which needs a bachelor's degree or higher plus 2 years' relevant experience, and a course-completion certificate such as a TEFL does not count as a degree.

faqs.q: Are public school jobs better than language centre jobs in Vietnam?
faqs.a: They suit different lives. Agency public-school work is weekday daytime with big classes and pay that largely stops from June to August; centre work is evenings and weekends with smaller classes and hours all year. Advertised hourly rates overlap.

faqs.q: Do I need a CELTA, or is a 120-hour TEFL enough?
faqs.a: For most centres a 120-hour TEFL is enough, and VUS accepts online courses. CELTA or an equivalent is asked for at the top of the market, such as RMIT and British Council teacher posts, and international schools want a teaching licence instead.

faqs.q: Is ACET or Apax Leaders still hiring teachers?
faqs.a: No. IDP's ACET stopped operating in Vietnam on 31 December 2024, and the Apax Leaders chain collapsed in 2023–24 owing wages. Older guides and job boards may still list them.

faqs.q: Will Vietnam's English-as-a-second-language plan create more jobs for foreign teachers?
faqs.a: Possibly, but not yet. Decision 2371/QĐ-TTg (October 2025) mainly trains and recruits Vietnamese teachers and only orders research into letting English-proficient foreigners teach in public schools, and HCMC's 246-school direct-hire pilot had produced no job ads by October 2026.

faqs.q: Can I start teaching while my work permit is being processed?
faqs.a: No. Working before the permit is issued is working without one, which since 10 September 2026 means a fine under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP and possible deportation, and the employer is fined too.
